evidence: Nestled along the windswept dike road of the Red River, Hang Tre Street stands as a vibrant junction at the periphery of Hanoi’s historic Old Quarter. Historically, this alluvial plain served as a bustling docking point for rafts laden with bamboo, luong, and nua from upstream regions, which were transported downstream to supply essential building materials for the entire imperial city.

A prominent feature is the imposing concrete dike wall that stretches alongside the road, enclosing one side of the bustling thoroughfare. Nestled beneath lush tree canopies, Hang Tre Street remains a vital part of Hanoi’s cultural tapestry, seamlessly blending historical significance with contemporary vibrancy.
